summary: You have produced a strong, coherent preliminary report, with a clear Australian mission rationale, a feasible project plan and useful early orbital work. You are already at the Accomplished level across the criteria; there is no higher rubric band. The next steps will make your imaging, coverage and delivery claims more rigorously supported and strengthen the report further.
next_steps: Assess whether 10 m imagery can reliably identify bleaching: specify relevant sensor bands, consider water-column effects and turbidity, and explain how you will validate performance against the cited mapping method.
Use orbit-access simulations to test weekly reef coverage and 24-hour delivery, accounting for latitude, revisit, daylight and cloud availability; estimate data volume and downlink capacity.
Show the J2 calculation and assumptions behind the 97.8° inclination, and add task completion criteria to the Gantt plan so progress and feasibility can be checked.

criteria.C1: In Mission Concept & Rationale, you clearly connect reef monitoring to Australian users, including AIMS, and state measurable objectives. To strengthen this Accomplished work, substantiate the 10 m requirement by addressing sensor bands, water-column effects, turbidity and validation against the cited mapping method.
criteria.C2: Your Project Plan and Image 1 provide a mission-linked sequence, deadlines and contingencies; Information Sources identifies relevant resources. Strengthen the plan by defining completion criteria for tasks and showing how orbit, sensor and downlink feasibility results will inform later design decisions.
criteria.C3: Preliminary Progress shows useful hand calculations and an initial STK scenario, and you identify the swath-versus-coverage trade. Show the J2 derivation and assumptions for the 97.8° inclination, then simulate coverage and assess daylight, cloud constraints, data volume and downlink before treating weekly coverage and 24-hour delivery as feasible.
criteria.C4: Your logical structure, readable prose, labelled tables and figure, and matching reference list make the report easy to follow. For an even more polished presentation, revise awkward phrasing and describe sources precisely while keeping citations and formatting consistent.
